Subject: Hosted API pricing qualification — Orchid Health: monthly tokens & peak TPS (next steps)

Hi Lauren / Dev —

Thanks again for the call earlier — helpful to see the workflow and where Redwood would sit in your content pipeline. To keep momentum and get a pricing sketch over to procurement, can you confirm the two items we discussed? I captured our notes below.

Quick recap from my side:
- Primary integration: real-time consumer support assistant and scheduled batch summaries (nightly digest).
- Sensitive data scope: PHI in prompts — you indicated EHR PII will be stripped at source; will need SOC2 + KMS for Private later, but for now this is Hosted API to validate integration.
- Key asks: expected monthly token volume, expected peak TPS (30s window), and budget range target ($/month or $/1M tokens).

What we talked about you sharing:
1) A realistic monthly tokens estimate for the first 6 months (low / likely / high).
2) Typical peak TPS during business hours (5-minute and 30-second peak windows if possible).
3) Any hard budget ceilings or target unit economics (e.g., target $/1M tokens or monthly spend cap).

If you can reply with those three items I’ll run a quick unit-econ model and send a 2-page pricing sketch and an attached estimate workbook (orchid_estimate_v1.xlsx) for procurement. Tentative next steps:
- Jordan/Marissa: send pricing sketch within 24 hours of your numbers
- Procurement: review and flag any billing constraints / preferred PO cadence
- If numbers align, slot a 30-min procurement + engineering call next week to walk RBAC/KMS in more detail.

Thanks — Jordan

--
Jordan Blake

Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing qualification — Orchid Health: monthly tokens & peak TPS (next steps)

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. Below are the numbers we can commit to right now based on the project plan and dev estimates. We tried to give conservative / likely / optimistic ranges for monthly tokens.

Monthly tokens (first 6 months):
- Low: 5M tokens / month (pilot: 2 clinics)
- Likely: 18M tokens / month (Q1 after pilot, 8 clinics)
- High: 50M tokens / month (full rollout, additional triage features)

Peak traffic windows:
- 5-minute peak: ~120 reqs/minute (average request ~800 tokens) -> ~1.6k TPS equivalent tokens during peak 5-min window.
- 30-second peak (burst): we see spikes up to ~50 reqs/30s -> ~1.3k tokens/30s in worst-case simulated load. Note: our front-end batches some messages into 1 call for summaries which increases token-per-request variance.

Budget guidance: current procurement target is $20k–$45k / month for the POC-to-initial-rollout phase. Their ask: aim for unit economics near $0.90–$1.25 per 1M tokens (they used that phrasing when we discussed) — they understand market ranges, but want to see a plan to get to ~$1/1M as usage scales.

Attached is a quick traffic extract (summary rows) — will follow up with the infra team if you need raw logs.

Hope that helps — happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk list items.

Best,
Lauren
Head of Integrations, Orchid Health
lauren@orchidhealth.com

Thanks Lauren — perfect, this is exactly what we need. Quick clarifications before I finalize the sketch:
1) When you say "average request ~800 tokens", can you confirm whether that includes both prompt + expected response tokens? (We typically price per-token consumed so we want to align on definitions.)
2) For the 30s burst, you said "50 reqs/30s" — is that concurrent independent requests, or are those short bursts caused by retries from your frontend?

If you can confirm those two bullets I’ll send a pricing sketch with three scenarios (pilot / scale / full rollout) and an estimated monthly invoice for each, plus a recommended rate band aimed at your $0.90–$1.25 / 1M target. If we can get to the ~$1/1M target with a commit or volume banding, I’ll note the required minimums in the sheet.

Proposed 30-min follow-up: Fri 12:00pm PT if that works for procurement/infra? I’ll include Marissa and Karthik for the unit-econ and SLO questions.

Jordan
